{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mo-f","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"5e155e89847a66f0357b4a0d2dad276d000e16fd650018c088beeaf4e7dec86d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mo-class-f:lineage:23","source_registry_sha256":"f128002157e581eb7004b9370c8cfbafd7b29a1596262980704fbda0a45932f5","source_liveness_sha256":"fdf72d02e75b9589fee5aaf5b83ec9705ff03586f574464e3553a827f9b698d8"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Missouri parking: safe parking habits, no-parking zones, handicapped parking, hill parking and parallel parking","heading":"C — Parking: safe placement and securing the vehicle, exiting safely, no-parking zones, handicapped spaces and penalties, parking on hills and the parallel parking steps","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Parking: safe placement and securing the vehicle, exiting safely, no-parking zones, handicapped spaces and penalties, parking on hills and the parallel parking steps
Knowledge domain: where and how to park so the vehicle is not a hazard, how to secure it and leave it safely, the places parking is forbidden, the rules for spaces marked with the International Symbol of Access, the checklist for parking on a hill, and the order of steps for parallel parking.

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A01
Once parked, your vehicle must not become a hazard, so leave it far enough from any travel lane that it does not get in the way and where drivers coming from either direction can see it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A01
Use a designated parking area whenever you can. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A01
On a one-way street you may usually park on either the left or the right side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A01
Every time you park, set the parking brake, and leave a manual transmission in gear or an automatic in park. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A01
Look for traffic before opening your door, get out on the curb side when possible, and have passengers, especially children, leave on the curb side too. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A01
Before opening a door, watch for cyclists, who often ride along the right edge of the travel lanes next to parked cars, and close the door as soon as you are out. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A01
Never leave the keys in a parked vehicle, and lock it any time it will be out of your sight. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A01
If you have to park on the roadway itself, get as far from traffic as you can, and pull as close as possible to the curb if there is one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A01
When parked on a hill, turn the wheels sharply toward the side of the road so that a rolling car moves away from traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A01
Look for signs that ban or limit parking, and note that some limits are shown by colored curb markings. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A01
Never park inside an intersection, on a crosswalk or sidewalk, or across the entrance to a driveway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A01
Do not park on the left side of a two-way street or with your vehicle facing against the flow of traffic. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A01
Parking is forbidden next to a curb painted yellow, on a bridge, or in front of a fire hydrant. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A01
Do not park where your vehicle blocks normal traffic or creates a hazard for other drivers. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A01
A handicapped space may be used only by a vehicle showing a disability placard or plates, and only while a person with a physical disability is in it or is being dropped off or picked up. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A02
The International Symbol of Access marks spaces reserved for vehicles driven by or carrying people with disabilities. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A02
A conviction for misusing a handicapped space brings a fine of at least $50 and no more than $300. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A02
Parking in the striped access aisle beside a handicapped space is illegal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A02
Using someone's disability placard or plates to take a handicapped space is illegal when that person is not riding along at the time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A02
Before leaving a car parked on a hill, turn the wheels the proper way, shut off the engine with the vehicle in the proper gear, and set the parking or emergency brake. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A02
To finish leaving a car parked on a hill, take the keys out, check the rearview mirror for traffic before stepping out, then lock the car and keep the keys with you. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A02
Before pulling out of any parking space, check traffic and signal. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A02
To begin parallel parking, stop alongside the car in front of the empty space, about 1½ feet to its left. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A02
Next, turn the wheels sharply right and back slowly into the space, making sure your front end does not block passing or oncoming traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A02
Once your front clears the car ahead, turn the wheels sharply left and keep backing, then turn sharply right and pull forward toward the curb, ending in the middle of the space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0038]

Misconceptions: a handicapped placard does not let anyone park in a reserved space when the person it belongs to is not being carried; the striped aisle next to a reserved space is not extra parking; you may park on either side of a one-way street but not on the left side of a two-way street.
Mnemonics: brake, gear, keys, lock before you walk away; for parallel parking think right, left, right as you back in and straighten.
Glossary: International Symbol of Access means the wheelchair symbol marking reserved parking; access aisle means the striped space beside a reserved space used for getting in and out; parallel parking means parking in line with the curb between two vehicles.
Dynamic facts: the handicapped parking fine range is statutory and can change, and cities may post their own parking limits and curb colors that must be checked locally.
